citation: Vincent C. Hinck, William M. Clark Jr., Carl E. Hopkins. Normal interpediculate distances (minimum and maximum) in children and adults. Vol. 97, No. 1, May 1966, pp. 141-153 (the journal title is not printed on the article pages; American Journal of Roentgenology, Radium Therapy and Nuclear Medicine by inference from volume, year, pagination and refs. 3 and 7). Source: thread "Reread every paper for clinical detail", project symphony_4, 2026-10-28. Copy read: greg's upload of 2026-10-28 01:02 UTC (upload id 436d54c9-898b-42e7-bb47-4eab21fd218b; a second upload is the same paper), sha256 begins 2c4dc4ab2b91585b.
population: USA, Portland, Oregon: white living hospital patients found by a systematic search of the University of Oregon Medical School's radiograph files, films taken for other purposes; 474 AP spine roentgenograms: 353 of children under 19 yr in seven groups (3-5 yr 35, 6-8 yr 52, 9-10 yr 30, 11-12 yr 46, 13-14 yr 59, 15-16 yr 63, 17-18 yr 68; mean ages 4.1 to 17.5 yr) and 121 of adults (>18 yr, upper age not stated). Counts by sex never given (Inference from the means: male share about 0.36-0.67 by group, 0.44 in adults). Films screened for readability and an attempt made to exclude significant anomalies and growth-affecting problems. Per-level N 8 (child cervical) to 68; adults 36 (C3) to 60 (C7). Substudy: 10 randomly selected normal patients aged 10-15 yr with AP thoracic spine and PA chest films, 89 paired measurements of a possible 120 (p. 141-142, 145, 148; PDF 1-2, 5, 8).
modality: AP spine roentgenograms at a 40 in (101.6 cm) target-film distance, magnification neither stated nor corrected (film values); calipers read to 0.1 mm by one author; patient position for the main series not stated (substudy AP thoracic film recumbent). Substudy adds erect PA chest films at 72 in (p. 141, 148; PDF 1, 8).
levels_covered: C3 to L5, 22 vertebrae; C1 and C2 excluded as unmeasurable, sacrum omitted for an inadequate sample (p. 142, PDF 2). How levels were identified and numbered, rib counts and transitional segments are not described.

anomalies.variant: Lumbosacral transitional vertebra, sacralisation, lumbarisation, L6, T13, 11 or 13 rib pairs, cervical ribs
anomalies.finding: Not mentioned anywhere; no prevalence of any numerical or transitional variant is reported.
An attempt was made to eliminate subjects with significant anomalies and other problems likely to influence growth; no count of exclusions and no definition.

anomalies.variant: Hemivertebra at T2 and ventral hemivertebra at T10, with basilar invagination and partial atlanto-occipital assimilation (osteochondrodystrophy)
anomalies.finding: Single illustrative case (Case IV, boy 3 6/12 yr): gross IPD decrease in the lower thoracic spine (graph, approximate: T9 11, T10 8.8, T11 10.5 mm, below the 3-5 yr floor of 12-13; spike at T8 about 16.4; L4 16.0 and L5 15.4 below the 18 and 21 floors) with a marked increase of the midsagittal diameter at the same level; asymptomatic; the caption notes variable vertebral body size.
anomalies.how_identified: Roentgenograms; Fig. 8A is an AP thoracic view; which films showed each anomaly is not said

anomalies.finding: Single case (Case II, boy 5 1/2 yr, referred for mental retardation, no signs of stenosis): IPDs below T10 at or beyond the lower 90 per cent limit, stenosis greatest at lower lumbar and sacral levels; graph (approximate) L1 17.0, L2-L3 16.4, L4 17.4, L5 15.5 mm against 3-5 yr limits 17-24 to 21-28; sagittal diameters diminished.
anomalies.how_identified: AP lumbar spine films; lateral for sagittal diameter

anomalies.finding: Single case (Case III, girl about 4 yr): massive vertebral bone, especially pedicles, narrowing every IPD shown (graph, approximate, T7 8.8 to L5 15.9 mm, 3-5 mm below the 3-5 yr band) while keeping the normal shape; lumbar sagittal diameters diminished; no clinical findings.

anomalies.variant: Developmental transverse canal stenosis from decreased IPD (the authors call it an anomaly)
anomalies.finding: Exists, may or may not accompany a decreased sagittal diameter, may be symptomatic; its frequency is unknown. Case I, a 60-year-old man, thoracic stenosis especially T5-T10 with T7 and T8 at the adult lower limit, symptomatic with cord signs.
anomalies.how_identified: AP spine films measured against the norms; myelography

measures.name: Interpediculate distance (IPD)
measures.definition: Shortest distance between the medial surfaces of the two pedicles of a vertebra, read with calipers to 0.1 mm on the AP film (p. 141, PDF 1). Inference: the medial cortical margins of the end-on pedicle shadows.
measures.projection: AP radiograph, 40 in target-film distance, uncorrected for magnification; PA chest usable below T3 with moderate accuracy; not obtainable from a lateral
measures.level_pattern: Adult means (Table IA): C3 28.0, C4 28.8, C5 29.4, C6 29.3, C7 28.0; T1 24.0, T2 20.5, T3 18.8, T4 18.1, T5 17.6, T6 17.3, T7 17.4, T8 17.7, T9 18.2, T10 18.7, T11 20.2, T12 23.2; L1 25.0, L2 25.5, L3 26.0, L4 26.9, L5 29.7 mm. Cervical plateau peaking at C5-C6; drop C7 to T1 -4.0 and T1 to T2 -3.5 (about 2 SDs each); flat thoracic minimum T4-T10, lowest T6; rise T11 to T12 +3.0 (1.6 SD); T12 to L1 +1.8 and L4 to L5 +2.8 (under 1 SD); L1-L3 nearly flat. At every age: C7/T1 -2.4 to -4.5, T1/T2 -3.2 to -3.7, T11/T12 +2.0 to +3.0, L4/L5 +2.8 to +3.8 mm; T12/L1 only +0.6 at 3-5, 6-8 and 13-14 yr. Thoracic minimum at T5-T7 at every age; cervical maximum at C5 or C6 (computed from Table IA).
measures.covariates: Sex: males larger by about 1 mm (text); adult male-female 0.4 (T11) to 2.2 (C7) mm, mean 1.25 (computed); girls exceed boys at several cervical and lumbar levels at 11-12 and 13-14 yr. Age: growth from 3-5 yr to adult 3.6-4.1 mm cervical, 1.4-3.3 thoracic, 4.5-5.2 lumbar (computed; text says 3 to 5 mm); thoracic and lumbar growth mostly before 9-10 yr, cervical continuing to 13-14 yr. Size: individuals differ more in the overall level of the profile than at single vertebrae (p. 146). Population: white Oregon patients only. SD by level (adult): 1.5-2.0 cervical and thoracic, 2.2 (L1) to 3.7 (L5); 11-12 yr group most variable (boys' SDs 3 mm or more).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: in the vertebra's local frame, isolate the pedicles (SPINEPS arch subregion voxels between the posterior body wall and the front of the articular processes, where the ring is closed); project them along the AP axis onto the coronal plane; per craniocaudal row take the gap between the most medial points of the two pedicles; IPD is the smallest gap over rows crossing both pedicles. The true axial alternative is the minimum left-right gap between the medial pedicle walls in any axial slice. Exclude laminae, lateral recess and mid-body canal width. Multiply true size by film magnification (about 1.07-1.17 at 40 in, Inference) before comparing with Hinck.
measures.radiograph_recipe: AP film or AP fluoroscopy: caliper the narrowest gap between the medial cortices of the left and right pedicle shadows at each level C3-L5; values are on the film scale (Hinck's at 40 in, uncorrected); M = SID/(SID - OFD) (Inference); axial rotation foreshortens it (Inference). PA chest films read about 1.1 mm smaller at T1-T3 and about 0.4 mm smaller at T4-T12 than AP spine films (10 patients aged 10-15 yr).
measures.error: Intra-observer duplicates (89 pairs in 9 cases): median absolute difference 0.26 mm, mean 0.40, range 0 to 3.6; 10 per cent zero, 50 per cent under 0.26, 75 per cent under 0.50, 90 per cent under 1.0 mm (Inference: per-reading SD about 0.27 mm with a heavy tail). No inter-observer study. Resolution 0.1 mm.
measures.page: p. 141-147 (PDF 1-7); Tables IA, IB, IC, II; Figs. 1-3

measures.name: 90 per cent tolerance range of IPD (lower and upper normal limits)
measures.definition: For each vertebra and age group, limits within which the central 90 per cent of normals should fall (5 per cent below, 5 per cent above), sexes combined, in whole mm: mean +/- k SD with SDs and Ns averaged over similar vertebrae and k = 2.8, 2.5, 2.3, 2.1 for N = 10, 15, 20, 30 from Dixon and Massey (Inference: two-sided normal tolerance factors at 95 per cent confidence).
measures.covariates: One set per age group, sexes pooled because the sex effect is an order of magnitude below age (p. 144).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: put a CT-derived IPD on the film scale (magnification) before comparing.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Compare each measured AP IPD with its age group's limits and also compare the shape of the whole profile with the normal curve (p. 146).
measures.error: Carries the sampling error of small groups (as few as 8 films per level in children).

measures.name: Interperson SD of IPD
measures.definition: SD of IPD by level and age group, sexes combined, with N (Table II).
measures.level_pattern: Cervical about equal (text 1.4-2.8, table 1.2-2.8); thoracic least at T3-T10, T1, T2, T11, T12 slightly more; lumbar rising with age, L4 and L5 uniformly more variable than L1-L3 because in a few normals they are smaller; adult CV about 5-6 per cent C3-C6, 7.5-9.7 thoracic, 12.5 at L5 (computed).
measures.covariates: Most variable at 11-12 yr (boys, growth-spurt timing); slight rise with age, attributed to harder visualisation and size differences; slight thoracic rise at 13-14 yr.
measures.error: Includes reading error (about 0.27 mm SD, Inference).

measures.name: AP spine minus PA chest IPD (projection effect)
measures.definition: Per thoracic vertebra, IPD on the AP recumbent thoracic spine film (40 in) minus IPD on the erect PA chest film (72 in), same patient.
measures.level_pattern: Table IV: T1 1.46 (N 8), T2 1.06 (8), T3 0.79 (8), T4 0.58 (9), T5 0.38 (10), T6 0.08 (9), T7 0.31 (8), T8 0.64 (7), T9 0.22 (5), T10 0.20 (8), T11 0.58 (6), T12 0.43 (3) mm; mean T1-T3 1.10, T4-T12 0.38, general 0.57. Largest at T1, smallest at T6, explained by kyphosis and shoulder posture changing object-film distance.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: a magnification-geometry effect; models how a projected IPD shifts with position and object-film distance along a curved column.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Chest films not recommended but usable with moderate accuracy below T3.

measures.name: Sagittal (midsagittal) diameter of the canal
measures.definition: Named only, not measured or defined here; referenced to cervical and lumbar stenosis work (refs. 3, 4, 5, 10).
measures.projection: Lateral radiograph (Inference from Case I, where a minimally rotated lateral hid it)
measures.level_pattern: Diminished in Cases II and III; markedly increased at the level of the narrowed IPD in Case IV; no values.

level_details.detail: Not measurable on AP films; excluded.

Plateau peaking at C5-C6 (adult 29.4, 29.3; 3-5 yr 25.3, 25.3); least represented region; cervical growth continues to 13-14 yr; girls aged 3-5 show an irregular curve rising to C7, put down to small subgroup samples.
Largest drop of the profile: adult 28.0 to 24.0 to 20.5 mm (about 2 SDs each), present at every age; sex difference largest at C7 (2.2) and T1 (2.0 mm, computed).
AP-PA chest discrepancy largest (1.10 mm mean); chest films least reliable there.
Narrowest and least variable canal by IPD; minimum T6 (adult 17.3, 3-5 yr 15.8); adult lower limit 14 mm at T5-T7, 12 mm at T4-T10 at 3-5 yr; Case I stenosis especially T5-T10.

Adult T10 18.7, T11 20.2, T12 23.2, L1 25.0; T11/T12 rise +2.0 to +3.0 at every age, T12/L1 only +0.6 at 3-5, 6-8 and 13-14 yr (computed). Case I had a persistent left extradural defect at T12-L1 at myelography.
Nearly flat (adult 25.0, 25.5, 26.0); at 3-5 yr L2 20.4 slightly below L1 20.5.

Largest lumbar step (adult 26.9 to 29.7); L4 and L5 the most variable levels (adult SD 3.0, 3.7) and occasionally smaller than L1-L3 in normals; widest tolerance ranges (adult 21-33, 23-37; 13-14 yr 19-33, 22-36).
No norms (sample inadequate); achondroplastic stenosis greatest at lower lumbar and sacral levels in Case II.

errors.value: 89 duplicates in 9 cases, made independently at different times by the one measuring author
0.40 mm, raised by a few extremes

errors.what: Range and distribution of duplicate differences
errors.value: 0 to 3.6 mm; 10 per cent zero, 50 per cent under 0.26, 75 per cent under 0.50, 90 per cent under 1.0 mm

errors.what: Projection effect AP spine (40 in) vs PA chest (72 in)
errors.value: Mean 0.57 mm larger on AP; 1.10 at T1-T3, 0.38 at T4-T12; 1.46 at T1, 0.08 at T6
Not stated or corrected; norms are film values at 40 in (Inference: about 1.07-1.17)

pearls_pitfalls.text: Maximum norms serve the diagnosis of intraspinal tumour; minimum norms the recognition of canal stenosis; any carefully measured IPD outside the limits raises suspicion of pathology or anomaly.
The limits are an index of suspicion only: they will not catch every anomaly, and a value inside them does not guarantee normality.
Normal spines share one IPD profile; a vertebra or adjacent pair distinctly out of line is suspicious even inside the limits, so compare the shape of the patient's curve with the normal.
Transverse stenosis from a small IPD exists, may or may not accompany a small sagittal diameter, and may be symptomatic; it was virtually unexplored, its frequency unknown.

Case I (60-yr man): abdominal wall weakness first taken for a right flank hernia, lancinating pains, gait and leg weakness, absent ankle jerks, CSF protein 84 mg per cent; IPDs narrow T5-T10 with T7 and T8 at the lower limit; myelography with slow hesitant thoracic transit and a T12-L1 extradural defect. Smallest IPDs at, not below, the limits do not argue against stenosis; the stenotic distribution overlaps the normal.
Children with more striking stenosis (achondroplasia, osteopetrosis, osteochondrodystrophy) were asymptomatic, attributed to the immature nervous system's capacity to compensate during growth.

Enlarged pedicles (osteopetrosis) narrow the IPD; achondroplasia narrows it below T10, most at lower lumbar and sacral levels; a hemivertebra region showed focal IPD collapse with a widened sagittal diameter.
Pitfall: C1-C2 unmeasurable on AP films; no sacral norms.
Pitfall: films taken for other purposes often omit part of the spine; chest films obscure some vertebrae (89 of 120 pairs usable).
Pitfall: chest PA and spine AP IPDs are not interchangeable at T1-T3; acceptable with moderate accuracy below T3.
Pitfall: a minimally rotated lateral film hid the sagittal diameter in Case I.
Pitfall: in normals L4 and L5 are occasionally smaller than L1-L3, so a lumbar reversal alone is weak evidence.
Pitfall: children vary most at 11-12 yr (growth-spurt timing); use the age group's limits.
Pitfall: norms are for white patients at 40 in; another distance and position shift them (AP-PA study); other populations untested (Inference).
Limitation admitted: clinical experience of transverse stenosis still limited; minimum standards are a preliminary to studying its frequency and significance.

instructions.text: On an AP radiograph or AP fluoroscopy frame, for each vertebra C3-L5 with visible pedicles, measure the shortest distance between the medial cortices of the left and right pedicles, in mm on the film scale.
Do not attempt IPD at C1 or C2, and do not compare sacral IPD with these norms.
Never derive IPD from a lateral view; the lateral gives the sagittal diameter, a separate quantity.

Put measurements on Hinck's scale before comparing: his are uncorrected film values at 40 in; multiply a true CT width by an assumed magnification (Inference: about 1.07-1.17) or compare adjacent-level ratios, which largely cancel magnification except along the curved thoracic column.

From a CT instance mask, project the pedicle voxels along the vertebra's AP axis and take the narrowest left-right gap between the medial pedicle edges over the rows crossing both pedicles; exclude laminae and body (Inference).

Use the profile as a level cue: cervical plateau peaking at C5-C6, drops of about 4 mm C7 to T1 and 3.5 mm T1 to T2, flat minimum T4-T10 lowest at T6, rises of about 1.5, 3.0 and 1.8 mm at T10/T11, T11/T12 and T12/L1, flat L1-L3, jump of about 2.8 mm at L4/L5 (adult).
Do not expect IPD to separate neighbours within T4-T10 or within L1-L3; the differences are under one SD.

In a child, do not rely on a T12/L1 step (only 0.6 mm at 3-5, 6-8 and 13-14 yr); use T11/T12 (+2.0 to +3.0), C7/T1 (-2.4 to -4.5), T1/T2 (-3.2 to -3.7) and L4/L5 (+2.8 to +3.8), which hold at every age (Inference: arithmetic).
Choose limits by age group from Table III, sexes combined; expect males about 1 mm larger.

Flag an IPD below the lower limit as possible stenosis and above the upper limit as possible intraspinal mass or anomaly; flag a vertebra or adjacent pair out of line with the curve even inside the limits.
Do not clear a spine because all IPDs are inside the limits; Case I was symptomatic at the lower limit.

When lumbar IPD fails to widen caudally, L5 is below L4 and values below T10 sit at or under the floor, suspect achondroplasia-type stenosis and check the sagittal diameter on the lateral; the pattern also appeared in Case IV (Inference from Fig. 8B).
When pedicles look massive and dense and IPDs are uniformly narrow, consider osteopetrosis.
Where hemivertebrae or irregular body sizes appear, expect focal IPD collapse and possibly a widened sagittal diameter at that level; count levels with care.
If only a PA chest film is available, read IPD below T3 with moderate accuracy; at T1-T3 expect it about 1.1 mm below the AP spine value, about 0.4 mm below at T4-T12 (10 patients aged 10-15 yr).
Treat one IPD reading as carrying about 0.3 mm error (Inference) with occasional misreads of 1 to 3.6 mm; re-measure a value that sits alone off the curve.
Read a profile, not a value: normal spines share one shape and differ mainly in overall level.
In children, use the age group's own limits and expect the widest scatter at 11-12 yr and at L4-L5 at 13-14 yr.
Check axial rotation on AP views, which foreshortens the projected IPD (Inference); the paper warns of rotation only on the lateral.

bordercall: (a) Anomaly priors: none. No prevalence of any transitional, numerical or segmentation anomaly; significant anomalies were screened out (p. 141, PDF 1); Case IV's hemivertebrae are one case.

(b) Hinck's IPD is the minimum medial-pedicle distance as projected on an AP film at 40 in, magnified and uncorrected. A mask width taken at mid-body, at the lateral recess or as the canal's maximum width runs larger; one at the laminae runs smaller (Inference).

(b) Versus Panjabi's cadaveric SCW (widest canal width, true size; from the panjabi notes of this set, Inference): Hinck/Panjabi about 1.10 at T1, 1.00 at T6-T8, 1.05 at T12, 1.05 at L1, 1.10 at L5; versus Eisenstein's dry-bone greatest interpedicular distance (Caucasoid men) 1.13 at L1, 1.18 at L5, near his AP magnification 1.14. A level-dependent factor is needed before pooling film and bone values.

(b) Candidate additions: a film-equivalent projected IPD per level C3-L5 for radiographs and fluoroscopy; adjacent-level IPD ratios carrying the C7/T1, T1/T2, T11/T12 and L4/L5 junction signals; full thoracic profile T1-T12; paediatric age-group means from 3 yr (Table IA) with SDs (Table II).
(b) Emission: adult per-level mean and SD give a Gaussian IPD emission; discrimination concentrated at C7/T1 and T1/T2 (about 2 SDs), T11/T12 (1.6 SD); other steps under one SD (computed).

(c) Measurement error: reading SD about 0.27 mm (Inference from median duplicate difference 0.26 mm), heavy tail to 3.6 mm; AP-PA projection shift 0.6 mm mean, 1.1 at T1-T3; magnification unreported; Table II SDs include reading error.

(d) Sex: male about 1 mm larger (adult 0.4-2.2 by level, mean 1.25, computed); girls larger at several cervical and lumbar levels at 11-12 and 13-14 yr. Age: growth 3.6-4.1 cervical, 1.4-3.3 thoracic, 4.5-5.2 lumbar from 3-5 yr to adult, so a single size factor will not model growth (Inference). Size: shared overall profile level supports a patient size factor (p. 146). Population: white Oregon patients only.
gaps: Not given: counts by sex; adult upper age and age distribution; how levels were identified and numbered; transitional handling; object-film distance, magnification, patient position for the main series; inter-observer error; confidence level of the tolerance intervals; body size data.
Table II's Age row (.05 to .09) under an SD-in-mm heading has no clear meaning (Inference).
Text gives cervical SDs 1.4-2.8 mm but Table II has 1.2 (13-14 yr C3) and 1.3 (9-10 yr C4).
Text gives growth of about 3 to 5 mm from 3-5 yr to adult, but thoracic levels grow 1.4-3.3 mm by Table IA (computed).

At 11-12 yr the combined mean lies outside the male-female interval at C4 (27.0 vs 27.8, 27.4) and L4 (24.9 vs 23.6, 24.2); male T6 at 9-10 yr (18.8) is out of line (T5 17.4, T7 16.5; combined 16.5), likely a misprint (Inference).
Text says males are consistently larger, but girls exceed boys at C3, C5, C6, L4 (11-12 yr) and C3-C6, L2-L5 (13-14 yr; L5 30.4 vs 28.0).
Wide L4-L5 limits at 13-14 yr are attributed partly to small samples, yet N is 34 there, more than at 9-10 or 3-5 yr.
13-14 yr thoracic means exceed the 15-16 and 17-18 yr means (T7 18.2 vs 16.9, 17.5): a non-monotone age curve, not discussed (Inference: sampling).
Fig. 5B (Case I) shows no tolerance band in this copy; from the graph T2 is about 25.3 mm, above the adult upper limit 24, not mentioned by the authors (Inference). Fig. 8B's band is faint.
Inference: sex mix implied by where combined means fall: male share about 0.65 (3-5 yr), 0.54, 0.67, 0.58, 0.50, 0.36, 0.38, 0.44 (adult).

Against Panjabi and Eisenstein (sibling notes, Inference): no single magnification reconciles film and bone values (ratio 1.00 mid-thoracic to 1.18 at L5), and definitions differ (shortest vs greatest vs widest canal).
